      "observations": [
        "All six owned paths and all 887 normal-diff lines were read. The Graph present-item path now requires isRead, calls on_message_updated first, and falls back to on_message_created after any callback error. The source itself records that the error should later be restricted to message-not-found. This is broader than the fixed accepted match on NS_MSG_MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND; other current callback errors propagate. The neighboring folder-sync edit adds diagnostics and the same TODO without fixing that predicate in this landing.",
        "The owned Graph payload still supplies size 0 and isFlagged false, and uses an empty preview fallback. The native update handler skips a zero size, clears Marked when false and only writes a nonempty preview. The tests deliberately skip Graph size and flag assertions. This phase therefore does not establish complete size/flag/preview synchronization; it does not prove a reproduced flag-loss regression. Current Graph code later reads size and follow-up flag fields.",
        "EwsMessageSyncHandler::OnMessageUpdated finds the header by Exchange ID and returns NS_MSG_MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND when absent. For an existing header it removes a cached offline body, applies read/marked flags and parsed headers, then now notifies the database listeners with captured old flags and nullptr instigator before committing. Current ExchangeMessageSync retains the sequence and adds later reply-subject handling. Actual nsMsgDatabase::NotifyHdrChangeAll broadcasts only for a header present in the database; nsMsgDBView::OnHdrFlagsChanged refreshes matching rows when the instigator differs from the view. This supports this caller comment without proving that no other listener cares.",
        "Both native success and failure handlers now attempt SyncCounts and UpdateSummaryTotals before the existing stop callback. This accounts for earlier partial updates even when the operation fails. Each MOZ_TRY can return early, so the source does not promise an unconditional stop callback if count refresh itself fails. The existing partial-additions/final-status lesson remains the bounded foundation; no new runtime recovery result is claimed.",
        "The Graph fake now emits create/update/readflag changes in the same present-item shape, with isRead and To/Cc recipients, while deletes retain @removed. Its final delta token advances to the end of the global item-change stream rather than deriving a token from the last folder-filtered change. MockServer corrects created to create and also removes update/readflag entries whose last state in that requested range is delete. It still uses the existing slice/filter/truncation rules. Current fake code later delegates generic delta handling with a structured ChangePage and nextOffset; that is not this historical implementation.",
        "Three formerly EWS-only scenarios now also run for Graph: direct client updates, real-folder persistence and recipient storage. The shared client helper receives a protocol Boolean because EWS has separate read-status callbacks. The listener reset clears per-round observations/token/promise but preserves the known-created-ID set, allowing subsequent Graph update callbacks to identify existing messages. Its original unknown-ID exception is generic NS_ERROR_FAILURE because the Thunderbird error was not exposed through Cr; current tests later use the exact message-not-found code.",
        "The real-folder scenario uses protocol-specific source/destination folders, syncs hierarchy first and checks 6 to 4 total messages, 6 to 3 unread, a changed token, updated Subject/body greeting, changed store token, and a moved message in the destination. Graph size/flag checks are explicitly skipped. Recipient expectations remove every quote character, not only surrounding quotes; simple To/Cc display-name/address values are checked, not general RFC quoting or server equivalence. The inherited client assertion still counts deleted IDs against a two-element updated-ID array; it does not identify updated messages. Link the existing focused test-limit lesson rather than repeat it.",
        "The owned comments explain update-before-create recovery, old flags, external instigator, and failure-path count refresh. The explicit fourth-argument wording matches the actual call. Test helper JSDoc names the preserved reset state and protocol-specific read callback behavior. All changed JavaScript assertion messages are nonempty expected-behavior statements with should; scalar batching counts still use a deep assertion. This is scoped harness practice, not a global style mandate.",
        "Complete primary 2025009 and full D294706 creation-to-final timeline, all seven actual submitted old/current inline bodies and zero summary histories were read. Source C3 captured the review and Source A captured the Bug; this join reads retained bodies without new browser confirmation. Historical Try/remote-build events are not rerun.",
        "The author reports that header changes reached the database without refreshing the frontend and qualifies the EWS/MS365 effect through a separate ReadFlagChange path. The owned added notification is verified statically; it is not a reproduced real-server diagnosis. Reviewer asks what instigator means; the owned comment now identifies the fourth parameter passed as nullptr, and the actual current database/view receivers support this external-change role.",
        "The reviewer asks whether count and recipient-quoting differences also apply to EWS. The author qualifies count impact to EWS servers delivering read flags as Update changes and later attributes quoting to a separate Graph formatting path, opening 2033709. Owned source indeed formats recipients with a simple name/address string while the shared test removes quotes. That does not prove Microsoft server quoting or all RFC cases; the dependency remains unread.",
        "The initial create-on-any-update-error branch and generic JS unknown-ID exception are retained as this landing, distinct from current exact message-not-found handling. Later fields, generic mock pagination, required typed members and reply-subject changes are bounded current comparisons. The updated-identity assertion limitation links its existing focused lesson; it is not evidence that the new native update path fails at runtime."
